1	# Command-assembly split — per-cluster recipe
2	
3	Project trail: https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2619 (one change per cluster).
4	Base branch for all wave-1 work: `cor-2268-cmdutil` (adds `internal/cli/internal/cmdutil` with WriteJSON/WriteText/WriteTextToWriter/StickyErrorWriter — use these, never copy them).
5	
6	## Goal per cluster
7	
8	Move one command cluster out of package `cli` into `internal/cli/command/<name>`
9	(package `<name>`), exporting `New(opts base.Options) *cobra.Command` (plus
10	additional constructors if the cluster registers several commands). The root
11	assembler (`internal/cli/root.go`) imports the package and mounts the command;
12	nothing else in `cli` may import the new package unless it already called the
13	moved code. The new package must NOT import `internal/cli`.
14	
15	## Layering (already in place — use it, do not re-create it)
16	
17	- `internal/cli/internal/base` — env/XDG/store paths (`base.EntireEnv`,
18	  `base.Options`, `base.ResolvePluginDirs`, `base.BrainDirForKey`), redaction,
19	  safe reads, agent args. `cli.Options`/`cli.EntireEnv` are aliases of these.
20	- `internal/cli/internal/brainstore` — locks, atomic writes, privacy state
21	  (tombstones, transactions, read guard, retrieval policy), untrusted state
22	  readers, error-code taxonomy (`brainstore.MemoryErrorCode`, `*Code` consts).
23	- `internal/cli/internal/cmdutil` — command output helpers.
24	- `internal/cli/internal/clitest` — `clitest.PinXDGRoots` (every new test
25	  package MUST have `main_test.go` with `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { os.Exit(clitest.PinXDGRoots(m)) }`),
26	  `clitest.UseHostXDGDataHome`, shared fakes.
27	- `internal/cli/internal/patterntest` — corpus fixtures incl. `OpenCorpusMutableDB`.
28	- `internal/cli/patterns`, `internal/cli/workspace`, `internal/cli/entities` —
29	  feature logic. `workspace.DefaultStore(env)` is the store constructor.
30	
31	## Hard rules (from COR-2268; violations have failed CI before)
32	
33	1. **Never edit `internal/cli/main_test.go`'s `TestMain` declaration** — its
34	   normalized source SHA-256 is pinned in
35	   `tools/ci-bench/windows-production/settings.json`. Other decls in that file
36	   are editable. Do not touch anything under `tools/ci-bench/`.
37	2. **Tests move, not rewritten**: identical assertions and fixtures. Allowed
38	   edits: package clause, imports, symbol qualification forced by the move, and
39	   re-pointing a root-command invocation to the cluster's own constructor when
40	   the test exercises only this cluster (`NewRootCommand(opts)` +
41	   `cmd.SetArgs([]string{"<cmd>", ...})` → `<name>.New(opts)` +
42	   `cmd.SetArgs([...])` without the leading command word — keep the change
43	   minimal and obvious). A test that exercises several commands or root routing
44	   stays in `cli`.
45	3. **No shims**: never leave a `cli`-side function/const/var that merely
46	   forwards to the moved one — sed-rename the call sites. Type ALIASES in `cli`
47	   are allowed when they cut churn. A `cli`-side wrapper is allowed only when
48	   it binds a real `cli`-private dependency (precedent: `verifyDerivedClean`).
49	4. **Hook-seam vars** (`var x = func(...)` swapped by tests) get exactly ONE
50	   home. If a moved function reads one, the var moves (exported) and every
51	   swap site is renamed.
52	5. **Shared helpers sink, they don't duplicate.** If the cluster needs a
53	   `cli`-private helper that other `cli` code also uses, move it to the right
54	   internal package (base/brainstore/cmdutil/patterns/workspace) and rename ALL
55	   call sites. If the closure is large (>3 unexported helpers that are not
56	   obviously storage/output/env), STOP and report instead of improvising.
57	6. Keep one home for constants; export only what remaining callers need.
58	7. Comments move verbatim; update only identifier spellings inside them.
59	
60	## Mechanical sequence
61	
62	1. `git fetch origin` then branch from `cor-2268-cmdutil`:
63	   `git checkout -b cor-2268-cmd-<name> cor-2268-cmdutil`.
64	2. Record before-inventory:
65	   `go test ./internal/cli -list '.*' | grep -c '^Test\|^Benchmark\|^Example\|^Fuzz'`
66	   and save the sorted name list to a file.
67	3. Map the closure first: for every symbol the cluster's files reference that
68	   lives elsewhere in `cli`, decide move / sink / stays-with-adapter. Use
69	   `entire graph impact --repo . --head --format json --symbol <sym>` for
70	   exported/shared symbols and grep for the rest; cite what you checked in the
71	   final report. Compile early and often.
72	4. `git mv` the cluster's prod files to `internal/cli/command/<name>/`, set the
73	   package clause, export the constructor(s) (`newXCommand` → `New`, extra
74	   commands keep descriptive exported names). Qualify base/brainstore/cmdutil/
75	   patterns/workspace imports. Update `root.go` to `<name>.New(opts)`.
76	5. Create `internal/cli/command/<name>/main_test.go` (clitest pin) BEFORE
77	   moving any test file. Then `git mv` the cluster's test files; apply only the
78	   allowed edits.
79	6. Build + vet loop: `go build ./... && go vet ./...` until clean; then
80	   `gofmt -w -s internal/`.
81	7. Reconcile inventory: after-lists for `./internal/cli` and the new package;
82	   the union of names must equal the before-list exactly (TestMain is not a
83	   runnable root). Report moved-root names.
84	8. Verify moved bodies: diff each moved test function against its pre-move body
85	   normalized only for the rename map; report IDENTICAL/DIFFERS per root.
86	9. Gates, all mandatory, report real output:
87	   - `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli/command/<name>`
88	   - focused `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/cli -run '<ClusterPattern>'`
89	   - `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`
90	   - `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools/ci-bench/windows-production/tests -p 'test_*.py'`
91	   - `python3 -B tools/coverage/mutation_check.py`
92	   - full race suite `go test -race -p=1 ./... -count=1 -timeout=30m` (run it;
93	     if wall-clock is prohibitive in your environment, run
94	     `go test -race -count=1 -timeout=20m ./internal/cli` plus every other
95	     package, and SAY SO explicitly in the report).
96	10. Commit on your branch with explicit file paths (never `git add -A`), message
97	    `refactor(cli): move <name> command(s) into internal/cli/command/<name>`,
98	    ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
99	    Do NOT push, do NOT open PRs or trails — the orchestrator lands branches.
100	
101	## Report format (what you return)
102	
103	- Branch name + commit SHA.
104	- Moved files (prod/test), moved root names and count, inventory before/after
105	  numbers, body-comparison verdicts.
106	- Helpers sunk to shared packages (symbol → new home) with impact/grep evidence.
107	- Anything re-pointed from NewRootCommand (test name + one-line description).
108	- Gate results verbatim (pass/fail + durations). Anything skipped and why.
109	- Anything that did not fit the rules (left in cli, and why).

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). See Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ When `execute_code` is available, use it to read Datadog data, even for a single lookup: one script can make several API calls, join data across products, and return only what the answer needs. Skill guides still apply for domain knowledge (query syntax, attribute and metric names, pitfalls), but where a guide tells you to call a specific read tool such as `search_datadog_logs`, `analyze_datadog_logs`, or `get_datadog_metric`, make the equivalent call from `execute_code` instead, using `search_datadog_sdk` to find it. This takes precedence over tool choices in skill guides. Use the named tool only when `search_datadog_sdk` finds no operation for what you need, or when `execute_code` still fails for a step after following its own error guidance. This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. ## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, entire/trails before trail work, entire/querying for the full querying reference. Load them proactively, at the start of the work, not after an error.

Feedback: if a tool is wrong, misleading, or missing something, call send_entire_feedback (name the tool). Code search is gated per jurisdiction — where the index is not deployed, those tools say so.

  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

  setup              Build the brain and start background updates

  config             Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

  get                Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get          Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash               Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

  recall             Retrieve durable memories matching a query for the current branch
  remember           Record a durable memory about this repository
  distill            Extract durable memories from sessions (requires an agent)
  memories           Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable memories
  connect            Bind this repository to its hosted brain explicitly
  disconnect         Stop syncing this repository with its hosted brain
  verify             Verify durable memory anchors against local retained sources
  patterns           Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Code index & context:
  inspect            Explore code, dependencies, and change history
  show               Show one code-index record
  viz                Explore the brain as a graph in your browser

== cor-2268-cmd-connect
COR-2268 connect/disconnect extraction (branch cor-2268-cmd-connect) reuses the entities Config/Deps pattern for command packages: internal/cli/command/{connect,disconnect} export New(cfg Config) where Config embeds base.Options and Deps carries cli-bound operations (repoStoragePaths, agentSurfaceTarget, installPushHook/uninstallPushHook adapted, hostedFactsSyncAndPull adapted to (attempted, pullSucceeded bool), hostedSyncBranch), bound in internal/cli/connect_config.go. Sinks forced by types/shared use: hosted_binding.go -> brainstore (HostedRepoBinding + Read/Write/SetHostedOptOut), renderHostedBanner -> cmdutil, host-CLI trio (HostEntireBinary, HostedShellOutTimeout, DecodeHostCLIJSON) -> base, commandRunnerFunc test fake -> clitest.CommandRunnerFunc. The hosted sync engine (hosted_sync.go: loadFacts/writeFacts/feed cache/pull filter closure) and env.go repo-identity subsystem stay in cli — injecting them avoided a foundation-sized sink. publish was DEFERRED: its closure needs cli-private exportManifest, loadBrainManifest, loadSessionReadGuard/guardFactRecords, resolveManualHostedTarget/manualHostedTarget, facts path helpers, parseRepoRemote/normalizeRepoHost, runGitOutput, brainExportExists - types cross the boundary, so neither injection nor a small sink works until manifest/facts-store layers sink.

5 internal/cli/export.go
   1 internal/cli/facts.go
   1 internal/cli/skill_form.go

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"sort"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/base"
11		bmanifest "github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/manifest"
12		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
13	)
14	
15	// facts_integrity.go cross-checks the manifest's declared fact source against
16	// the facts the store can actually produce — both HOW MANY it produces and
17	// WHICH ones, because a corruption can leave the first right while destroying
18	// the second (see COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH below).
19	//
20	// sources.facts in the manifest is a CLAIM: "this brain holds N facts". Every
21	// health surface printed that claim as though it were an observation, and
22	// nothing ever compared it to the store. A facts.ndjson that had gone lossy —
23	// a line overwritten with valid JSON that is not a fact record, a truncated
24	// file, a botched hand edit — therefore kept reporting N on `status`, `doctor`
25	// and `facts map` while recall returned fewer, `get fact:<id>` said "not
26	// found", and `search` volunteered that the answer "may genuinely not be in
27	// the brain". For a durable-memory product that last line converts silent data
28	// loss into an affirmative false statement.
29	//
30	// The history index already solves this and its wording is the model:
31	//
32	//	history index size does not match the manifest; run `entire brain refresh
33	//	history` to rebuild it
34	//
35	// Note WHERE that check lives. It is not inside the per-record reader; it is
36	// in the function that loads the artifact the manifest declares, so every
37	// caller of that artifact inherits it and the REBUILD path — which must be
38	// able to run against the damaged artifact — does not. Facts need the same
39	// shape, and loadFacts is the wrong seam for three reasons:
40	//
41	//  1. loadFacts is per-branch and the manifest records only a total across
42	//     branches, so loadFacts cannot know what N is for the branch it is
43	//     reading.
44	//  2. Its ~30 callers include distill, remember, facts gc/promote/merge and
45	//     refresh — the very commands that REPAIR a lossy store. A loader that
46	//     failed closed would wedge the store shut with no way out.
47	//  3. The manifest's count is produced by loadAllFactBranches (see
48	//     updateFactSourceManifestLocked). Checking the claim with the same
49	//     function that produced it makes the check an exact inverse: no
50	//     branch-name-to-directory ambiguity, and any disagreement is real.
51	//
52	// So the check lives here, beside missingFactBranchStores — the existing seam
53	// for "the manifest names something the store cannot produce" — and every
54	// surface reads one report. The retrieval note inherits through the single
55	// emptyResultBlindSpot choke point, which covers recall, search, query and
56	// retrieve at once.
57	
58	// COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH. The first cut of this check compared Declared against
59	// Readable and nothing else, which leaves a corruption that PRESERVES the count
60	// completely invisible: overwrite one line of facts.ndjson with a copy of
61	// another and the store still yields N records, still parses, still declares N
62	// — and the fact whose line was taken is gone. `get fact:<id>` says "not
63	// found", doctor says "facts: ok", and `search` goes back to volunteering that
64	// the answer "may genuinely not be in the brain". That is the same affirmative
65	// false statement this file exists to eliminate, reached by a different route.
66	//
67	// The obvious repair — compare the declared id SET against the readable one —
68	// is not available: sources.facts records counts (facts/distilled/authored/
69	// superseded/by_kind), never ids, and putting ids there would not help. That
70	// manifest is re-derived from the store itself by summarizeFactSource on every
71	// remember, refresh, gc, promote and retract, so a declared id set would
72	// re-baseline onto the damage at the next write exactly as the count does, and
73	// would cry loss on every legitimate id-changing operation in between.
74	//
75	// What IS checkable from the store alone, with no bookkeeping and nothing that
76	// can go stale, is the invariant the store is written under: WITHIN ONE BRANCH
77	// AN ID IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE FACT. Every writer keys by id before it writes
78	// (factmerge.Upsert, factmerge.Promote via IndexOf, factmerge.GC), so a branch
79	// that yields the same id twice was not written by this program. The second
80	// record did not join the fact set; it stands where a different fact used to
81	// be. That is loss, and it is loss the count cannot see.
82	//
83	// Per BRANCH, emphatically not per brain. A fact id is sha256 of normalized
84	// text plus sorted paths (factmerge.RecordID) — the branch is not in it — so
85	// the same fact carried between branches keeps its id, which is precisely what
86	// `facts promote` does on purpose. A brain-wide id set would report data loss
87	// on every promote, and a check that cries loss on a legitimate operation is
88	// worse than the hole it closes.
89	
90	// factStoreDefectMode names WHICH way the store fails the manifest. They are
91	// different user situations and must not collapse into one sentence: "not
92	// built" is a rebuild, "corrupt" is a repair, "lossy" is data that is gone and
93	// has to be re-distilled, and "duplicated" is data that was overwritten while
94	// the numbers stayed right.
95	type factStoreDefectMode string
96	
97	const (
98		// factStoreDefectNone is a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
99		factStoreDefectNone factStoreDefectMode = ""
100		// factStoreDefectMissing: a declared branch has no facts.ndjson at all.
101		// Already detected by missingFactBranchStores; kept in its own words.
102		factStoreDefectMissing factStoreDefectMode = "missing"
103		// factStoreDefectUnreadable: a line will not parse. The store is corrupt
104		// and nothing on the branch can be read, not just the bad line.
105		factStoreDefectUnreadable factStoreDefectMode = "unreadable"
106		// factStoreDefectLossy: every line parses, but the store yields fewer
107		// facts than the manifest declares. This is the readable-but-short case —
108		// the one that used to pass every health surface.
109		factStoreDefectLossy factStoreDefectMode = "lossy"
110		// factStoreDefectStale: the store yields MORE facts than the manifest
111		// declares. Not data loss — the manifest is behind — but still a declared
112		// number that was never observed, so it is reported rather than printed.
113		factStoreDefectStale factStoreDefectMode = "stale"
114		// factStoreDefectDuplicated: every line parses and the counts are not
115		// short, but one branch stores the same fact id twice. Deliberately NOT
116		// folded into "lossy": lossy is a SHORTFALL — fewer facts than claimed,
117		// repaired by re-distilling what is missing — while this is a
118		// SUBSTITUTION, where the arithmetic is intact and a specific fact was
119		// overwritten by a copy of its neighbour. Telling the two apart is the
120		// difference between "some of your memory did not survive" and "this
121		// particular record is standing in for one that is gone".
122		factStoreDefectDuplicated factStoreDefectMode = "duplicated"
123	)
124	
125	// factStoreIntegrity is the cross-check result. The zero value is a healthy
126	// store, so callers may use it unconditionally.
127	type factStoreIntegrity struct {
128		// Declared is sources.facts.facts — what the manifest claims.
129		Declared int `json:"declared"`
130		// Readable is how many records the store actually yields that are facts:
131		// a record carrying an id. A line that parses as JSON but has no id (the
132		// canonical corruption in this defect) is counted in Unusable, never here,
133		// because it is unaddressable by `get`, invisible to recall, and dropped
134		// by every status/scope filter.
135		Readable int `json:"readable"`
136		// Pending is sources.facts.pending_reconcile — staged candidate records
137		// the manifest deliberately declares OUTSIDE Facts (summarizeFactSource
138		// books a factStatusCandidate under its own counter until the next
139		// distill reconciles it). The store yields those records, so every
140		// Readable-vs-Declared comparison must add Pending back or a brain with
141		// one staged candidate reports "the manifest is behind the store"
142		// forever, through the very refresh the warning recommends.
143		Pending int `json:"pending,omitempty"`
144		// Unusable counts records read from the store that carry no id. They are
145		// reported even when the counts happen to agree, because a manifest
146		// re-summarized from an already-damaged store would otherwise hide them.
147		Unusable int `json:"unusable,omitempty"`
148		// Distinct is how many DIFFERENT fact ids the store yields, summed across
149		// branches but counted within each one (a fact id does not include the
150		// branch, so `facts promote` legitimately stores one id on two branches —
151		// see the file header). In a store this program wrote, Distinct always
152		// equals Readable; anything less is a record that overwrote another.
153		Distinct int `json:"distinct,omitempty"`
154		// DuplicateIDs names the ids a single branch stores more than once, sorted
155		// so the report is stable. The full set is kept for JSON readers;
156		// the one-line warning names only the first few.
157		DuplicateIDs []string `json:"duplicate_ids,omitempty"`
158		// Missing names declared branches whose facts.ndjson is absent.
159		Missing []string `json:"missing_branches,omitempty"`
160		// ParseError is the first line the store could not parse, in the loader's
161		// own words ("parse facts.ndjson line 3: ...").
162		ParseError string `json:"parse_error,omitempty"`
163		// Unreadable names the declared branches whose facts.ndjson will not parse.
164		// loadAllFactBranches stops at the first bad line and does not say WHOSE
165		// it was; with several branches declared, that is the difference between a
166		// repair the user can aim and one they cannot.
167		Unreadable []string `json:"unreadable_branches,omitempty"`
168		// Mode is the classification; empty when the store is intact.
169		Mode factStoreDefectMode `json:"mode,omitempty"`
170	}
171	
172	// OK reports a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
173	func (r factStoreIntegrity) OK() bool { return r.Mode == factStoreDefectNone }
174	
175	// pendingClause names the staged-candidate share of the expected count, so a
176	// mismatch message whose arithmetic includes Pending still adds up on the page.
177	func (r factStoreIntegrity) pendingClause() string {
178		if r.Pending == 0 {
179			return ""
180		}
181		return fmt.Sprintf(" (+%d staged candidate(s))", r.Pending)
182	}
183	
184	// expected is every record the manifest accounts for: published facts plus
185	// staged candidates awaiting reconciliation. It is what the store must yield
186	// for the cross-check to call it intact.
187	func (r factStoreIntegrity) expected() int { return r.Declared + r.Pending }
188	
189	// Lost is how many declared facts the store cannot produce. Zero unless the
190	// store is short.
191	func (r factStoreIntegrity) Lost() int {
192		if r.expected() > r.Readable {
193			return r.expected() - r.Readable
194		}
195		return 0
196	}
197	
198	// Overwritten is how many stored records lost their place to another record's
199	// id. Zero unless a branch repeated an id.
200	//
201	// Kept separate from Lost() on purpose. Lost() measures the store against the
202	// manifest's COUNT, and a substitution is invisible to that measurement by
203	// construction: the count is exactly what the corruption preserved.
204	func (r factStoreIntegrity) Overwritten() int {
205		if r.Readable > r.Distinct {
206			return r.Readable - r.Distinct
207		}
208		return 0
209	}
210	
211	// factStoreDuplicateIDsShown caps how many colliding ids the single-line
212	// warning names. The complete list stays in DuplicateIDs; a warning that
213	// printed a hundred ids would push the repair off the end of the line.
214	const factStoreDuplicateIDsShown = 3
215	
216	// factStoreIDList renders at most factStoreDuplicateIDsShown ids and says how
217	// many it held back, so the line stays one line without implying the damage
218	// stopped where the list did.
219	func factStoreIDList(ids []string) string {
220		if len(ids) <= factStoreDuplicateIDsShown {
221			return strings.Join(ids, ", ")
222		}
223		return fmt.Sprintf("%s and %d more",
224			strings.Join(ids[:factStoreDuplicateIDsShown], ", "),
225			len(ids)-factStoreDuplicateIDsShown,
226		)
227	}
228	
229	// factsRepairHint is the repair for a store that lost content. Rebuilding the
230	// manifest alone would only re-baseline the loss, so the fact commands' own
231	// wording — refresh, then re-distill — is what gets named.
232	func factsRepairHint() string {
233		return "run `" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh") + "` and re-distill"
234	}
235	
236	// Warning renders the single caller-facing line, or "" when the store is
237	// intact. Each mode keeps its own words.
238	func (r factStoreIntegrity) Warning() string {
239		switch r.Mode {
240		case factStoreDefectMissing:
241			return missingFactStoreWarning(r.Missing)
242		case factStoreDefectUnreadable:
243			where := "memory store"
244			if len(r.Unreadable) > 0 {
245				where = "memory store for " + strings.Join(r.Unreadable, ", ")
246			}
247			return fmt.Sprintf(
248				"%s is corrupt: %s; the %d memory(ies) the manifest declares cannot be recalled — %s",
249				where, r.ParseError, r.Declared, factsRepairHint(),
250			)
251		case factStoreDefectLossy:
252			detail := fmt.Sprintf(
253				"memory count does not match the manifest: %d declared%s, %d readable",
254				r.Declared, r.pendingClause(), r.Readable,
255			)
256			if lost := r.Lost(); lost > 0 {
257				detail += fmt.Sprintf(" (%d lost)", lost)
258			}
259			if r.Unusable > 0 {
260				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d stored line(s) carry no memory id", r.Unusable)
261			}
262			// A store can be BOTH short and collided. Reporting only the shortfall
263			// would understate the damage — the overwritten fact is gone too, and
264			// it is not one of the ones the arithmetic accounted for.
265			if overwritten := r.Overwritten(); overwritten > 0 {
266				detail += fmt.Sprintf("; %d more record(s) repeat a memory id (%s)", overwritten, factStoreIDList(r.DuplicateIDs))
267			}
268			return detail + " — " + factsRepairHint()
269		case factStoreDefectDuplicated:
270			return fmt.Sprintf(
271				"memory ids are not unique: %d stored record(s) repeat an id the branch already holds (%s); an id identifies exactly one memory, so each repeat stands where another memory used to be and that memory can no longer be recalled; the manifest's %d were counted, not read — %s",
272				r.Overwritten(), factStoreIDList(r.DuplicateIDs), r.Declared, factsRepairHint(),
273			)
274		case factStoreDefectStale:
275			return fmt.Sprintf(
276				"memory count does not match the manifest: %d declared%s, %d readable; the manifest is behind the store — run `"+base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "refresh")+"`",
277				r.Declared, r.pendingClause(), r.Readable,
278			)
279		default:
280			return ""
281		}
282	}
283	
284	// inspectFactStore cross-checks a declared fact source against the store on
285	// disk. A nil source is a brain with no facts declared: nothing is claimed, so
286	// nothing can be lost, and the result is healthy. That is what keeps a
287	// genuinely empty brain from reporting loss.
288	func inspectFactStore(brainDir string, source *factSourceManifest) factStoreIntegrity {
289		if brainDir == "" || source == nil {
290			return factStoreIntegrity{}
291		}
292		report := factStoreIntegrity{Declared: source.Facts, Pending: source.PendingReconcile}
293	
294		// Mode 1 — not built. A declared branch with no facts.ndjson is the
295		// already-handled case; keep its more specific message rather than folding
296		// it into the count mismatch it would also produce.
297		if missing := missingFactBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(missing) > 0 {
298			report.Missing = missing
299			report.Mode = factStoreDefectMissing
300			return report
301		}
302	
303		// Mode 2 — corrupt. loadAllFactBranches is the same function
304		// updateFactSourceManifestLocked used to PRODUCE source.Facts, so a
305		// disagreement below is a real one and not a re-derivation artifact.
306		// Validate declared paths through the same guarded reader used by recall
307		// before the aggregate loader opens any of those stores.
308		if broken := unreadableFactBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(broken) > 0 {
309			report.ParseError = broken[0].Err.Error()
310			for _, store := range broken {
311				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, store.Branch)
312			}
313			report.Mode = factStoreDefectUnreadable
314			return report
315		}
316		byFile, err := loadFactStoreFiles(brainDir)
317		if err != nil {
318			report.ParseError = err.Error()
319			for _, broken := range unreadableFactBranchStores(brainDir, source) {
320				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, broken.Branch)
321			}
322			report.Mode = factStoreDefectUnreadable
323			return report
324		}
325		duplicated := map[string]struct{}{}
326		for _, records := range byFile {
327			// One `seen` per store FILE, never one for the whole brain: a file is
328			// the set `loadFacts` hands to recall, so a repeat within one file is
329			// the only shape that shadows a memory. The same id across files is
330			// ordinary: `facts promote` copies a record into another branch's
331			// store, and the hosted pull mirrors the repo feed into the current
332			// branch's store. Bucketing by the branch recorded on each record
333			// conflated those mirrors into one bucket and reported them as
334			// corruption (COR-2220).
335			seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(records))
336			for _, record := range records {
337				if !isFactRecord(record) {
338					report.Unusable++
339					continue
340				}
341				report.Readable++
342				if _, repeat := seen[record.ID]; repeat {
343					duplicated[record.ID] = struct{}{}
344					continue
345				}
346				seen[record.ID] = struct{}{}
347				report.Distinct++
348			}
349		}
350		if len(duplicated) > 0 {
351			report.DuplicateIDs = make([]string, 0, len(duplicated))
352			for id := range duplicated {
353				report.DuplicateIDs = append(report.DuplicateIDs, id)
354			}
355			sort.Strings(report.DuplicateIDs)
356		}
357	
358		// Mode 3 — readable but short (or long).
359		switch {
360		case report.Readable < report.expected(), report.Unusable > 0:
361			report.Mode = factStoreDefectLossy
362		// Mode 4 — readable, and the arithmetic is not short, but a branch holds
363		// one id twice. This runs BEFORE the stale test on purpose: a duplicate
364		// that was appended rather than written over also makes the store longer
365		// than the manifest, and "the manifest is behind the store — run refresh"
366		// is the one piece of advice that must not be given here. Refreshing
367		// re-derives the count from the collided store, declares it, and the
368		// brain goes quiet about a fact it can no longer produce.
369		case len(report.DuplicateIDs) > 0:
370			report.Mode = factStoreDefectDuplicated
371		case report.Readable > report.expected():
372			report.Mode = factStoreDefectStale
373		}
374		return report
375	}
376	
377	// inspectBrainFactStore is inspectFactStore for callers that hold only a brain
378	// directory. A manifest that will not load, or one declaring no fact source,
379	// is reported as healthy: "this brain has no facts" is not fact loss, and the
380	// manifest's own health is a separate check that owns that message.
381	func inspectBrainFactStore(brainDir string) factStoreIntegrity {
382		if brainDir == "" {
383			return factStoreIntegrity{}
384		}
385		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
386		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
387			return factStoreIntegrity{}
388		}
389		return inspectFactStore(brainDir, manifest.Sources.Facts)
390	}
391	
392	// errFactStoreIncomplete is the exit verdict for a read surface that rendered
393	// a fact view over a store the manifest says is short. The view itself is
394	// printed — hiding the survivors helps nobody — but the command exits nonzero
395	// so a script cannot read the output as complete, matching how a corrupt
396	// history index already behaves.
397	var errFactStoreIncomplete = errors.New("memory store cannot produce every memory the manifest declares")
398	
399	// reportFactStoreIntegrity prints the cross-check verdict for a fact read
400	// surface and returns the error that should end the command, or nil when the
401	// store is intact.
402	//
403	// In text mode the warning goes to stdout, ahead of the view it qualifies, so
404	// a reader who pipes stdout sees it beside the numbers it corrects. In JSON
405	// mode stdout belongs to the document and the warning goes to stderr instead;
406	// the nonzero exit is what a JSON consumer must key on.
407	func reportFactStoreIntegrity(cmd *cobra.Command, brainDir string, jsonOut bool) error {
408		integrity := inspectBrainFactStore(brainDir)
409		if integrity.OK() {
410			return nil
411		}
412		out := cmd.OutOrStdout()
413		if jsonOut {
414			out = cmd.ErrOrStderr()
415		}
416		fmt.Fprintf(out, "warning: %s\n", integrity.Warning())
417		return renderedCommandError{err: errFactStoreIncomplete}
418	}
419	
420	// isFactRecord reports whether a parsed line is actually a durable fact. The
421	// id is the fact's identity — content-derived at authoring time and the only
422	// handle `get`, recall, dedup and supersede have — so a record without one is
423	// not a fact, however well-formed its JSON. The manifest producer
424	// (summarizeFactSource) and this checker share this predicate so the declared
425	// number and the checked number can never disagree by definition.
426	func isFactRecord(record factRecord) bool {
427		return strings.TrimSpace(record.ID) != ""
428	}

15	// facts_integrity.go cross-checks the manifest's declared fact source against
16	// the facts the store can actually produce — both HOW MANY it produces and
17	// WHICH ones, because a corruption can leave the first right while destroying
18	// the second (see COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH below).
19	//
20	// sources.facts in the manifest is a CLAIM: "this brain holds N facts". Every
21	// health surface printed that claim as though it were an observation, and
22	// nothing ever compared it to the store. A facts.ndjson that had gone lossy —
23	// a line overwritten with valid JSON that is not a fact record, a truncated
24	// file, a botched hand edit — therefore kept reporting N on `status`, `doctor`
25	// and `facts map` while recall returned fewer, `get fact:<id>` said "not
26	// found", and `search` volunteered that the answer "may genuinely not be in
27	// the brain". For a durable-memory product that last line converts silent data
28	// loss into an affirmative false statement.
29	//
30	// The history index already solves this and its wording is the model:
31	//
32	//	history index size does not match the manifest; run `entire brain refresh
33	//	history` to rebuild it
34	//
35	// Note WHERE that check lives. It is not inside the per-record reader; it is
36	// in the function that loads the artifact the manifest declares, so every
37	// caller of that artifact inherits it and the REBUILD path — which must be
38	// able to run against the damaged artifact — does not. Facts need the same
39	// shape, and loadFacts is the wrong seam for three reasons:
40	//
41	//  1. loadFacts is per-branch and the manifest records only a total across
42	//     branches, so loadFacts cannot know what N is for the branch it is
43	//     reading.
44	//  2. Its ~30 callers include distill, remember, facts gc/promote/merge and
45	//     refresh — the very commands that REPAIR a lossy store. A loader that
46	//     failed closed would wedge the store shut with no way out.
47	//  3. The manifest's count is produced by loadAllFactBranches (see
48	//     updateFactSourceManifestLocked). Checking the claim with the same
49	//     function that produced it makes the check an exact inverse: no
50	//     branch-name-to-directory ambiguity, and any disagreement is real.
51	//
52	// So the check lives here, beside missingFactBranchStores — the existing seam
53	// for "the manifest names something the store cannot produce" — and every
54	// surface reads one report. The retrieval note inherits through the single
55	// emptyResultBlindSpot choke point, which covers recall, search, query and
56	// retrieve at once.
57	
58	// COUNTS ARE NOT ENOUGH. The first cut of this check compared Declared against
59	// Readable and nothing else, which leaves a corruption that PRESERVES the count
60	// completely invisible: overwrite one line of facts.ndjson with a copy of
61	// another and the store still yields N records, still parses, still declares N
62	// — and the fact whose line was taken is gone. `get fact:<id>` says "not
63	// found", doctor says "facts: ok", and `search` goes back to volunteering that
64	// the answer "may genuinely not be in the brain". That is the same affirmative
65	// false statement this file exists to eliminate, reached by a different route.
66	//
67	// The obvious repair — compare the declared id SET against the readable one —
68	// is not available: sources.facts records counts (facts/distilled/authored/
69	// superseded/by_kind), never ids, and putting ids there would not help. That
70	// manifest is re-derived from the store itself by summarizeFactSource on every
71	// remember, refresh, gc, promote and retract, so a declared id set would
72	// re-baseline onto the damage at the next write exactly as the count does, and
73	// would cry loss on every legitimate id-changing operation in between.
74	//
75	// What IS checkable from the store alone, with no bookkeeping and nothing that
76	// can go stale, is the invariant the store is written under: WITHIN ONE BRANCH
77	// AN ID IDENTIFIES EXACTLY ONE FACT. Every writer keys by id before it writes
78	// (factmerge.Upsert, factmerge.Promote via IndexOf, factmerge.GC), so a branch
79	// that yields the same id twice was not written by this program. The second
80	// record did not join the fact set; it stands where a different fact used to
81	// be. That is loss, and it is loss the count cannot see.
82	//
83	// Per BRANCH, emphatically not per brain. A fact id is sha256 of normalized
84	// text plus sorted paths (factmerge.RecordID) — the branch is not in it — so
85	// the same fact carried between branches keeps its id, which is precisely what
86	// `facts promote` does on purpose. A brain-wide id set would report data loss
87	// on every promote, and a check that cries loss on a legitimate operation is
88	// worse than the hole it closes.
89	
90	// factStoreDefectMode names WHICH way the store fails the manifest. They are
91	// different user situations and must not collapse into one sentence: "not
92	// built" is a rebuild, "corrupt" is a repair, "lossy" is data that is gone and
93	// has to be re-distilled, and "duplicated" is data that was overwritten while
94	// the numbers stayed right.
95	type factStoreDefectMode string
96	
97	const (
98		// factStoreDefectNone is a store that can produce what the manifest declares.
99		factStoreDefectNone factStoreDefectMode = ""
100		// factStoreDefectMissing: a declared branch has no facts.ndjson at all.
101		// Already detected by missingFactBranchStores; kept in its own words.
102		factStoreDefectMissing factStoreDefectMode = "missing"
103		// factStoreDefectUnreadable: a line will not parse. The store is corrupt
104		// and nothing on the branch can be read, not just the bad line.
105		factStoreDefectUnreadable factStoreDefectMode = "unreadable"
106		// factStoreDefectLossy: every line parses, but the store yields fewer
107		// facts than the manifest declares. This is the readable-but-short case —
108		// the one that used to pass every health surface.
109		factStoreDefectLossy factStoreDefectMode = "lossy"
110		// factStoreDefectStale: the store yields MORE facts than the manifest
111		// declares. Not data loss — the manifest is behind — but still a declared
112		// number that was never observed, so it is reported rather than printed.
113		factStoreDefectStale factStoreDefectMode = "stale"
114		// factStoreDefectDuplicated: every line parses and the counts are not
115		// short, but one branch stores the same fact id twice. Deliberately NOT
116		// folded into "lossy": lossy is a SHORTFALL — fewer facts than claimed,
117		// repaired by re-distilling what is missing — while this is a
118		// SUBSTITUTION, where the arithmetic is intact and a specific fact was
119		// overwritten by a copy of its neighbour. Telling the two apart is the
120		// difference between "some of your memory did not survive" and "this
121		// particular record is standing in for one that is gone".
122		factStoreDefectDuplicated factStoreDefectMode = "duplicated"
123	)

125	// factStoreIntegrity is the cross-check result. The zero value is a healthy
126	// store, so callers may use it unconditionally.

129		Declared int `json:"declared"`
130		// Readable is how many records the store actually yields that are facts:
131		// a record carrying an id. A line that parses as JSON but has no id (the
132		// canonical corruption in this defect) is counted in Unusable, never here,
133		// because it is unaddressable by `get`, invisible to recall, and dropped
134		// by every status/scope filter.

136		// Pending is sources.facts.pending_reconcile — staged candidate records

144		// Unusable counts records read from the store that carry no id. They are

147		Unusable int `json:"unusable,omitempty"`
148		// Distinct is how many DIFFERENT fact ids the store yields, summed across

150		// branch, so `facts promote` legitimately stores one id on two branches —

152		// equals Readable; anything less is a record that overwrote another.
153		Distinct int `json:"distinct,omitempty"`
154		// DuplicateIDs names the ids a single branch stores more than once, sorted
155		// so the report is stable. The full set is kept for JSON readers;

157		DuplicateIDs []string `json:"duplicate_ids,omitempty"`

159		Missing []string `json:"missing_branches,omitempty"`

162		ParseError string `json:"parse_error,omitempty"`

164		// loadAllFactBranches stops at the first bad line and does not say WHOSE

166		// repair the user can aim and one they cannot.
167		Unreadable []string `json:"unreadable_branches,omitempty"`
168		// Mode is the classification; empty when the store is intact.
169		Mode factStoreDefectMode `json:"mode,omitempty"`
170	}

176	// mismatch message whose arithmetic includes Pending still adds up on the page.

286	// nothing can be lost, and the result is healthy. That is what keeps a
287	// genuinely empty brain from reporting loss.
288	func inspectFactStore(brainDir string, source *factSourceManifest) factStoreIntegrity {
289		if brainDir == "" || source == nil {
290			return factStoreIntegrity{}
291		}
292		report := factStoreIntegrity{Declared: source.Facts, Pending: source.PendingReconcile}
293	
294		// Mode 1 — not built. A declared branch with no facts.ndjson is the
295		// already-handled case; keep its more specific message rather than folding
296		// it into the count mismatch it would also produce.
297		if missing := missingFactBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(missing) > 0 {
298			report.Missing = missing
299			report.Mode = factStoreDefectMissing
300			return report
301		}
302	
303		// Mode 2 — corrupt. loadAllFactBranches is the same function
304		// updateFactSourceManifestLocked used to PRODUCE source.Facts, so a
305		// disagreement below is a real one and not a re-derivation artifact.
306		// Validate declared paths through the same guarded reader used by recall
307		// before the aggregate loader opens any of those stores.
308		if broken := unreadableFactBranchStores(brainDir, source); len(broken) > 0 {
309			report.ParseError = broken[0].Err.Error()
310			for _, store := range broken {
311				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, store.Branch)
312			}
313			report.Mode = factStoreDefectUnreadable
314			return report
315		}
316		byFile, err := loadFactStoreFiles(brainDir)
317		if err != nil {
318			report.ParseError = err.Error()
319			for _, broken := range unreadableFactBranchStores(brainDir, source) {
320				report.Unreadable = append(report.Unreadable, broken.Branch)
321			}
322			report.Mode = factStoreDefectUnreadable
323			return report
324		}
325		duplicated := map[string]struct{}{}
326		for _, records := range byFile {
327			// One `seen` per store FILE, never one for the whole brain: a file is
328			// the set `loadFacts` hands to recall, so a repeat within one file is
329			// the only shape that shadows a memory. The same id across files is
330			// ordinary: `facts promote` copies a record into another branch's
331			// store, and the hosted pull mirrors the repo feed into the current
332			// branch's store. Bucketing by the branch recorded on each record
333			// conflated those mirrors into one bucket and reported them as
334			// corruption (COR-2220).
335			seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(records))
336			for _, record := range records {
337				if !isFactRecord(record) {
338					report.Unusable++
339					continue
340				}
341				report.Readable++
342				if _, repeat := seen[record.ID]; repeat {
343					duplicated[record.ID] = struct{}{}
344					continue
345				}
346				seen[record.ID] = struct{}{}
347				report.Distinct++
348			}
349		}
350		if len(duplicated) > 0 {
351			report.DuplicateIDs = make([]string, 0, len(duplicated))
352			for id := range duplicated {
353				report.DuplicateIDs = append(report.DuplicateIDs, id)
354			}
355			sort.Strings(report.DuplicateIDs)
356		}
357	
358		// Mode 3 — readable but short (or long).
359		switch {
360		case report.Readable < report.expected(), report.Unusable > 0:
361			report.Mode = factStoreDefectLossy
362		// Mode 4 — readable, and the arithmetic is not short, but a branch holds
363		// one id twice. This runs BEFORE the stale test on purpose: a duplicate
364		// that was appended rather than written over also makes the store longer
365		// than the manifest, and "the manifest is behind the store — run refresh"
366		// is the one piece of advice that must not be given here. Refreshing
367		// re-derives the count from the collided store, declares it, and the
368		// brain goes quiet about a fact it can no longer produce.
369		case len(report.DuplicateIDs) > 0:
370			report.Mode = factStoreDefectDuplicated
371		case report.Readable > report.expected():
372			report.Mode = factStoreDefectStale
373		}
374		return report
375	}
376	
377	// inspectBrainFactStore is inspectFactStore for callers that hold only a brain
378	// directory. A manifest that will not load, or one declaring no fact source,
379	// is reported as healthy: "this brain has no facts" is not fact loss, and the
380	// manifest's own health is a separate check that owns that message.
381	func inspectBrainFactStore(brainDir string) factStoreIntegrity {
382		if brainDir == "" {
383			return factStoreIntegrity{}
384		}
385		manifest, err := bmanifest.Load(brainDir)
386		if err != nil || manifest == nil || manifest.Sources == nil {
387			return factStoreIntegrity{}
388		}
389		return inspectFactStore(brainDir, manifest.Sources.Facts)
390	}
391	
392	// errFactStoreIncomplete is the exit verdict for a read surface that rendered
393	// a fact view over a store the manifest says is short. The view itself is
394	// printed — hiding the survivors helps nobody — but the command exits nonzero
395	// so a script cannot read the output as complete, matching how a corrupt
396	// history index already behaves.
397	var errFactStoreIncomplete = errors.New("memory store cannot produce every memory the manifest declares")
398	
399	// reportFactStoreIntegrity prints the cross-check verdict for a fact read
400	// surface and returns the error that should end the command, or nil when the
401	// store is intact.
402	//
403	// In text mode the warning goes to stdout, ahead of the view it qualifies, so
404	// a reader who pipes stdout sees it beside the numbers it corrects. In JSON
405	// mode stdout belongs to the document and the warning goes to stderr instead;
406	// the nonzero exit is what a JSON consumer must key on.
407	func reportFactStoreIntegrity(cmd *cobra.Command, brainDir string, jsonOut bool) error {
408		integrity := inspectBrainFactStore(brainDir)
409		if integrity.OK() {
410			return nil
411		}
412		out := cmd.OutOrStdout()
413		if jsonOut {
414			out = cmd.ErrOrStderr()
415		}
416		fmt.Fprintf(out, "warning: %s\n", integrity.Warning())
417		return renderedCommandError{err: errFactStoreIncomplete}
418	}
419	
420	// isFactRecord reports whether a parsed line is actually a durable fact. The
421	// id is the fact's identity — content-derived at authoring time and the only
422	// handle `get`, recall, dedup and supersede have — so a record without one is
423	// not a fact, however well-formed its JSON. The manifest producer
424	// (summarizeFactSource) and this checker share this predicate so the declared
425	// number and the checked number can never disagree by definition.
426	func isFactRecord(record factRecord) bool {
427		return strings.TrimSpace(record.ID) != ""
428	}

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

walkers from facts_manifest.go. safePathComponent sinks to

guard. The shared-decoder and brain-spelling source scans widen to

## Report — stores wave 2: durable-facts store → `internal/cli/internal/factstore`

**Branch + commit:** `cor-2268-facts-store` (base `cor-2268-manifest-schema`), commit `76e0a204`. Not pushed. 154 files changed.

**Preflight/evidence:** Brain v0.3.0-17 and Graph entire-graph v0.6.0 both available and capability-checked. Brief ran; its semantic code-context was unavailable (search store not built for this commit) — Graph impact queries themselves worked and were used. Facts recalled (branch-scoped, found via `multi-get --branch`): fact:5a998dfa (manifest surface, `bmanifest`), fact:160632ec (cmd-facts deferral this unblocks, on `cor-2268-cmd-facts`), fact:972b6b79 (publish deferral, on `cor-2268-cmd-connect`). Brain went down mid-session (plugin symlink pointed at a deleted dev binary in the miami workspace); it recovered before finish and the closing memory was recorded as fact:c04f2531.

**Moved (prod):**
- `facts.go` → `factstore/factstore.go` (path helpers, Load/Write, taxonomy, SummarizeSource, store warnings)
- `facts_integrity.go` → `factstore/integrity.go` (Integrity/Inspect/InspectBrain/IsFactRecord/RepairHint/Defect modes)
- `facts_locus.go` → `factstore/locus.go` (ScopeOf, InferKind, KindOrInferred, Reclassify, FilterBy*, LocusOverlap*)
- `LoadStoreFiles`/`WriteStoreFile`/`LoadAllBranches` out of `facts_manifest.go` → `factstore/files.go`
- `factOriginImported` (one home) out of `facts_import.go`

**Helpers sunk:** `safePathComponent` → `base.SafePathComponent` (impact: callers only export.go ×5, skill_form.go ×1, facts.go — all renamed). Impact was run per exported-to-be symbol (~40 symbols); every caller is inside internal/cli, so no external blast radius. `writeFacts` impact needed disambiguation: a `verifyFixture.writeFacts` method exists; method declaration and `f.writeFacts(...)` call sites were deliberately left untouched.

**Stayed in cli (bindings, per rules):** `reportFactStoreIntegrity` + `errFactStoreIncomplete` (cobra + cli-private `renderedCommandError`), `factsRelevantToChange` (binds `semanticRecord`), manifest-update layer (`updateFactSourceManifest*`, `reclassifyAllFactBranches`, `preserveFactDistillEvidence` — bind `writeBrainManifestAndReadme`), proposals I/O (`reconcile.go`), guard composition (`loadSessionReadGuard`/`guardFactRecords` in session_privacy.go — no store function called the guard, so no adapter was needed). No shims; all ~380 call sites sed-renamed to `factstore.X`. No hook-seam vars in moved files.

**Tests:** clitest-pinned `main_test.go` created first; 14 store-level roots moved (5 from facts_test.go, 9 from facts_locus_test.go) into external package `factstore_test`. All 14 verified IDENTICAL under the published rename map (cli map + alias qualifications factRecord→factmerge.Record etc.). facts_integrity_test.go stayed whole (cli fixtures: semanticTestEnv/repoStoragePaths). Nothing re-pointed from NewRootCommand. Inventory: before 3185 = after 3171 (cli) + 14 (factstore), exact.

**Landmines flagged:** two source-scan guards widened minimally with the manifest-wave precedent — `versioned_state_test.go` decoder-scan dir list and `runnable_remedies_test.go` remedy walk now include `internal/factstore`. Manifest-writer regex untouched (writers stay in cli). Pinned TestMain and tools/ci-bench untouched.
